column3: Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
“Livestock” is rendered “possessions,” and “service” as “servants.”
“Made a feast” is rendered “hold a feast.”
“Had gone round” is rendered “had completed their cycle.” The Hebrew says “blessed God,” a euphemism; NASB renders “cursed God.” “All the days” is rendered “continually.”
“The adversary” is rendered as the name “Satan.”
“The adversary” is rendered “Satan,” and “roving about” as “roaming about.”
“Set your heart on” is rendered “considered.”
“In vain” is rendered “for nothing.”
“Put a hedge behind” is rendered “made a hedge about,” and “livestock” as “possessions”; “spread out” is rendered “increased.”
“If not … he will bless you” is an oath form with a euphemism; NASB renders “he will surely curse You.”
“In your hand” is rendered “in your power.”
“The day” is rendered “on the day when,” and “the firstborn” as “oldest.”
“On their hands” is rendered “beside them.”
“Sabeans fell” is rendered “the Sabeans attacked,” and “the mouth of the sword” as “the edge of the sword.”
“This one … this one” is rendered “he … another also.”
“Companies” is rendered “bands,” and “the mouth of the sword” as “the edge of the sword.”
“Until” is rendered “While … still.”
“There!” is rendered “behold,” and “the youths” as “the young people.”
Close to the Hebrew.
“Has taken” is rendered “has taken away.”
“Ascribe unseemliness to God” is rendered “blame God.”
